name: Self-Directed Queries Complexity of Singletons
proof: For any $S\subseteq[n]$, predict zero until a positive label identifies its singleton target; all subsequent labels can then be predicted correctly. If there is no positive label in $S$, no mistake occurs. Thus every finite-subset game costs at most one. For $n\ge2$, choose $S=[n]$: whichever coordinate the learner presents first, either prediction can be contradicted by a singleton target, so one mistake is necessary. At $n=1$ the sole target is known and every label is predictable without mistakes.
